Do not breastfeed during and for 2 weeks after therapy
No specific adjustment (limited data in severe impairment)
Use caution; discontinue for severe hepatic impairment
LFTs, pulmonary symptoms (ILD), skin, diarrhea, eyes
summary: Gefitinib is an oral EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor for first-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) mutations. Dosed 250 mg once daily, it commonly causes diarrhea and acneiform rash. Serious risks include interstitial lung disease, hepatotoxicity, GI perforation, and ocular and severe skin reactions.
indications: First-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations as detected by an FDA-approved test

dosage.d: 250 mg orally once daily with or without food
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: Withhold up to 14 days for Grade 3+ diarrhea, skin reactions, ALT/AST elevations or worsening respiratory symptoms, then resume
dosage.n: Discontinue for confirmed ILD, GI perforation, persistent ulcerative keratitis, severe hepatic impairment

dosage.d: Consider increasing to 500 mg once daily
dosage.n: Resume 250 mg 7 days after stopping the inducer

admin: Confirm EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutation by an FDA-approved test before starting
Take 250 mg orally once daily with or without food at about the same time each day
Do not take a missed dose within 12 hours of the next dose
For patients with swallowing difficulty, disperse the tablet in 4-8 ounces of water (stir ~15 minutes) and drink immediately or give by NG tube, then rinse
Monitor for and promptly evaluate new respiratory, hepatic, GI, ocular and skin symptoms
moa: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) drives growth and survival of NSCLC cells, particularly those with activating mutations (exon 19 deletion, exon 21 L858R). Gefitinib reversibly inhibits the tyrosine kinase activity of wild-type and certain mutant EGFR, blocking autophosphorylation and downstream signaling and thereby inhibiting EGFR-dependent tumor proliferation. It binds mutant EGFR with higher affinity than wild-type.

relative: Pre-existing interstitial lung disease or pulmonary fibrosis
History of GI perforation risk (diverticulitis, concurrent steroids/NSAIDs/anti-angiogenics)
Pre-existing keratitis or severe dry eye
monitor: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors
Drugs that raise gastric pH (PPIs, H2 blockers) - reduced absorption

preg: Based on mechanism and animal data, gefitinib can cause fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the final dose.
lact: Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided; there is limited data in severe renal impairment, so use with caution.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity can occur; obtain periodic liver function tests, withhold for Grade 2 or higher ALT/AST elevations, and discontinue for severe hepatic impairment. Exposure is higher in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment due to tumor involvement or cirrhosis.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin) - markedly reduce gefitinib levels; consider increasing dose to 500 mg/day
Drugs that sustainedly raise gastric pH (PPIs, H2 antagonists) - reduce gefitinib absorption and efficacy
Warfarin - elevated INR and bleeding events; monitor INR
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole) - increase gefitinib exposure and toxicity
Drugs causing GI perforation risk (corticosteroids, NSAIDs, anti-angiogenic agents) - additive perforation risk
CYP2D6 substrates - gefitinib may increase their levels
minor: Antacids - separate dosing to limit absorption interference
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit (CYP3A4 effect) in large amounts.
interactions.alcohol: Limit due to potential additive hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate transaminases and bilirubin; monitor LFTs.

serious: Bullous and exfoliative skin disorders (Stevens-Johnson, TEN)
emergency: Acute interstitial lung disease (new/worsening dyspnea, cough, fever)

monitoring: Periodic liver function tests (withhold for Grade 2+ ALT/AST elevations)
Respiratory symptoms - investigate promptly for ILD and discontinue if confirmed
Skin and mucosal reactions; diarrhea severity and hydration
Ocular symptoms (eye pain, redness, vision change) - withhold for severe/worsening, discontinue for persistent ulcerative keratitis
counsel: Take one 250 mg tablet once daily, with or without food, at about the same time each day
Report new or worsening shortness of breath, cough or fever immediately (lung inflammation)
Report severe diarrhea, severe skin rash/blistering, eye pain or vision changes
Use effective contraception during and for 2 weeks after treatment; do not breastfeed
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially acid-reducing drugs and warfarin
pk: Tumor response over weeks of therapy
Plasma peak ~3-7 hours after oral dose
Steady state in ~10 days; once-daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C
pearls: Interstitial lung disease is a potentially fatal warning - withhold for worsening respiratory symptoms and discontinue if ILD is confirmed
Only for tumors with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutation by an approved test; not for other EGFR mutations
Acid-suppressing drugs (PPIs/H2 blockers) reduce absorption and efficacy
With strong CYP3A4 inducers, increase the dose to 500 mg/day; revert to 250 mg 7 days after stopping the inducer
Monitor LFTs, skin, diarrhea, eyes and INR (warfarin) during therapy
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember, but do not take it within 12 hours of the next scheduled dose - skip it then and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses to make up.
overdose: There is no specific treatment for overdose; adverse reactions (such as diarrhea and rash) may be more frequent and severe. Manage symptomatically with supportive care and monitoring of hepatic, pulmonary, GI and skin toxicity.
